This is the module's own documented characteristic (header comment, sram_controller.sv:6-8: 'the flat array synthesizes to ~32K flip-flops plus a huge combinational 1024:1 read mux' -- the WRITE-side per-bit decode is structurally the same class of problem, not called out by name but architecturally identical). u_gpu/m_axi_wvalid is the SAME net bead je8/86a's earlier diagnosis (RUN_2026-09-13_23-34-16 vs run 23) found fans out to 18584 endpoints post-repair (37.6x more than run 23's 494) -- a fabric-wide shared control signal, present in BOTH flat (run 5/run 23) and deferred_flatten (run 8) synthesis, so the hierarchy mode is NOT the primary driver of the fanout size. CONCLUSION: this endpoint only becomes the frozen worst violator DURING repair -- the setup-repair algorithm's own buffer/resize actions on OTHER endpoints sharing this same physical buffer tree (the only way to reach thousands of endpoints from one driver) collaterally degrade this endpoint's slack, and the algorithm then oscillates trying to re-fix it without escaping, because every local fix perturbs the shared tree's loading and can un-fix a sibling endpoint. This is a genuine, single-cycle, same-domain (sys_clk->sys_clk) functional timing path -- s_wvalid gates a real write commit -- so an SDC false-path/multicycle exception would hide a real path and is NOT applied (per explicit instruction). A synthesis-side hierarchy change is not well-supported: the same net's fanout blowup was already present in run 5's FLAT synthesis (vs run 23's flat baseline), so deferred_flatten is unlikely to be the fix, and a full resynthesis experiment is far too slow to test within this iteration's time budget. This leaves resizer-settings as the only tractable lever: revert GATE_CLONING to true (attempt 1 proved this is needed, not harmful) and MAX_BUFFER_PCT to the default 50 (attempt 1's 15% cap was never binding -- only ~190 buffers were ever placed -- so it added no benefit and is removed), and additionally lower PL_RESIZER_SETUP_SLACK_MARGIN from 45 to 5 ps (still a real, deliberate ps value per bead s9f discipline, not an accidental near-zero) to reduce the total repair workload on already-marginally-passing endpoints elsewhere in the design, leaving more of the bounded wall-clock budget for the genuinely difficult shared-tree endpoints. If this still does not converge in reasonable time, the true fix is architectural (RTL: give the write-enable/index decode more real buffering headroom, or move this design off the flat per-bit-flop array for ASAP7/FreePDK45 flows the way SRAM_SKY130 already does for Sky130) -- out of scope for this task's authorisation (no RTL edits); that finding should be reported, not worked around further with config knobs.
